Structural survival of cliques across stricter density thresholds

Source: R/clique_stability.R
clique_threshold_sweep.Rd

Convenience wrapper that re-runs the full comparison-to-clique pipeline (compare_neighborhoods() -> summarize_comparison() -> comparison_to_edges() -> find_cliques()) at progressively stricter thresholds. For custom threshold logic, call the individual functions directly.

Usage

clique_threshold_sweep(
  cliques,
  target_species,
  networks,
  orthologs,
  multipliers = c(1.5, 2, 3, 5, 10),
  min_species = length(target_species),
  n_cores = 1L,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

cliques

Baseline output of find_cliques().

target_species

Character vector of species abbreviations.

networks

Named list of compute_network() outputs, keyed by species abbreviation. Each element must have $network (named numeric matrix) and $threshold (scalar).

orthologs

Data frame with columns gene1, gene2, hog.

multipliers

Numeric vector of threshold multipliers (each > 1). Default c(1.5, 2, 3, 5, 10).

min_species

Minimum species per clique (default length(target_species)).

n_cores

Cores for compare_neighborhoods() (default 1).

seed

Integer seed for the pi0 draws, or NULL (default) to draw from the global RNG. A seed makes the sweep reproducible.

Value

A list with components:

survival

Data frame with one row per (baseline clique, multiplier), including multiplier = 1.0 baseline rows where all cliques trivially survive: clique_idx (1-based), hog, multiplier, survived (logical), jaccard, n_species_orig, n_species_new.

sweep_cliques

Named list of find_cliques() outputs keyed by multiplier.

sweep_edges

Named list of combined edge data frames keyed by multiplier.

persistence

Data frame with one row per baseline clique: clique_idx, hog, birth (lowest multiplier where the clique exists; 1.0 for all baseline cliques), death (first multiplier above birth where the clique is lost; NA if it survives all tested multipliers), persistence (death - birth; NA if death is NA).

Details

No permutations are involved. The sweep uses the same q-values as find_coexpressologs(), with randomized-p pi0.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
sweep <- clique_threshold_sweep(cliques, target_species, networks,
  orthologs,
  multipliers = c(1.5, 2, 5)
)
# Survival curve
sapply(
  sort(unique(sweep$survival$multiplier)),
  function(m) mean(sweep$survival$survived[sweep$survival$multiplier == m])
)
} # }
